title: Annotations and Reflection
summary: Code that describes and inspects code - the built-in annotations, writing your own with @interface, retention and targets, reading annotations and members at run time with reflection, calling methods and creating objects by name, and the costs that come with it.

cards.q: Why must an annotation read by reflection have `@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)`?
cards.a:
Other retention policies drop the annotation before the program runs, so reflection never sees it

`SOURCE` annotations vanish after compiling and `CLASS` ones are in the class file but invisible at run time; only `RUNTIME` ones reach `getAnnotation`.

cards.q: A method called through `Method.invoke` throws `IllegalStateException`. What does the caller receive?
cards.a:
An `InvocationTargetException` whose `getCause()` is the `IllegalStateException`

`invoke` wraps whatever the method throws; unwrap it with `getCause()` to get the real exception.

cards.q: Which returns a class's private methods too?
cards.a:
`getDeclaredMethods()`

`getDeclaredMethods` lists every method declared in the class itself, whatever its access; `getMethods` lists only public ones, inherited ones included.
